title: Carnegie Endowment says a breach at its online donation vendor exposed contact and donor information
date_note: Date Carnegie disclosed it, per Nextgov; the intrusion at the vendor is dated 28 to 30 October.
geo_basis: organisation's home city; the source states no street location
summary: According to Nextgov, which reviewed an email notice, Carnegie said an intruder breached its online donation vendor from 28 to 30 October and accessed some information in its donor database. Carnegie said it included names, email addresses, phone numbers and, for donors, giving histories, and that full credit card information was not exposed. It described the affected contacts as a small percentage and gave no count.
plain: Carnegie says a hacker got into a vendor that handles its online donations and saw contact details and donor giving histories. It says full credit card numbers were not exposed.
exec: A supplier's breach exposed a think tank's donor and contact data, which could be used to craft convincing messages posing as the organisation.
action: Treat unexpected emails, calls or texts claiming to be from Carnegie with caution, as its notice advises.

validation.note: One publisher (Nextgov/FCW) relaying an email notice from Carnegie that it reviewed; the notice itself was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, data types, credit-card statement, no count, confirmed status and action against the Nextgov/FCW article
